headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can exfiltrate and act on content while mem0 provides no isolation, creating default data-leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 has no documented input isolation or provenance controls, while next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and MCP/browser/file inputs. If mem0 outputs are copied into next-ai-draw-io, attacker-controlled text can be reinterpreted as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not documented as default bridging, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF mem0 outputs are pasted or imported into next-ai-draw-io as prompt text
IF next-ai-draw-io processes file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a manual copy-paste review step before sending mem0 output to next-ai-draw-io
Prefix imported text with explicit 'data only' delimiters
Disable MCP inputs for the session
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management system and next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress plus API-key handling. If mem0 stores sensitive notes and next-ai-draw-io ingests them, its default outbound API calls can transmit that content to third-party model providers. The pairwise leakage path is credible from the profiles alone, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF mem0 contains sensitive notes or secrets
IF next-ai-draw-io sends imported document text to any external model API
mitigations: Keep sensitive mem0 collections out of the shared workflow
Route next-ai-draw-io to a local-only model backend
Remove API keys from the session before processing mem0 content
Review outbound requests for copied text before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-collection access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 is read-only from the profile except for memory management, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad network/API activity. They do not show the same filesystem write surface, but both can mutate shared knowledge artifacts if connected through the same workspace or MCP path. Uncertainty about the shared mutable surface pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or MCP resource
IF next-ai-draw-io writes diagram or text files that mem0 also indexes
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Run only one writer at a time for shared artifacts
Turn off concurrent instances during edits
requires-engineering: add locking around shared files or MCP resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly uses natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, so it can treat upstream text as actionable content. mem0 can supply remembered facts or summaries that next-ai-draw-io may render into diagrams or downstream API calls. Without a verification step, errors or hallucinations from mem0 can cascade into user-visible artifacts, making high appropriate.
conditions: IF mem0 output is used as authoritative input to next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io renders or acts on that output without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before rendering mem0-derived content
Add a verification checklist for imported facts
Mark mem0 output as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: insert a validation layer between agents

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 does not declare data classes or residency controls, while next-ai-draw-io handles files, images, and API keys and can send content to external providers. If regulated content is stored in mem0 and then processed by next-ai-draw-io, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0
IF next-ai-draw-io forwards that data to external APIs or retains it longer than policy allows
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Check retention settings before processing
Use a local model backend for regulated content
Document deletion/export handling for both tools
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
